research_question: Which established or emerging scientific and medical expressions need domain knowledge to interpret, and where do they occur in the selected documents?
inclusion_criteria: Collect domain-specific methods, conditions, measurements, abbreviations, and technical expressions, including established jargon.
Retain full expressions and precise spans, including useful multiword terms. A technical definition quoted from the source is stronger evidence than a proposed gloss.
Preserve distinct senses and document/page locations; terminology collection is not clinical advice.
Include a single grounded occurrence and preserve discoveries from either extractor.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude ordinary function words and general vocabulary requiring no domain knowledge in its supplied context.
Exclude isolated bibliography metadata, author names, and identifiers used only as labels unless a researcher explicitly broadens this recipe.
Do not infer diagnoses, efficacy, or medical recommendations from a term's occurrence.

positive.text: Heteroplasmy means that cells contain more than one mitochondrial DNA variant.
positive.sense: coexistence of more than one mitochondrial DNA variant
positive.reason: Established medical jargon is explicitly within scope.

positive.text: Retrieval-augmented generation combines retrieved documents with model generation in this fictional methods note.
positive.sense: generation that combines retrieved documents with model output
positive.reason: A technical multiword method name with a contextual explanation.

negative.text: The researchers read the paper on Monday.
negative.reason: Everyday vocabulary, not a domain-specific concept.

negative.text: The bibliography lists Rae Example as an author.
negative.reason: An author name used solely as metadata.

boundary.reason: A medical document alone does not turn general vocabulary into jargon; include a specialized contextual sense if supported.

boundary.text: The table labels a column PCR without expanding the abbreviation.
boundary.reason: The observed abbreviation may be collected, but an absent expansion must remain unavailable rather than source-confirmed.

technical_category.description: Model suggestion: method, condition, measurement, abbreviation, or other.

reader_difficulty.description: Optional model hypothesis about lay-reader difficulty; requires human validation.

abbreviation_expansion.description: Expansion when supported by the source; unavailable when absent.

specialist_lenses.lens: Attend to established medical jargon, full multiword expressions, and uncommon abbreviation senses while retaining all qualifying terms.
Attend to scientific method names, measurement terminology, and explained techniques while retaining all qualifying terms.
